concrete_findings.finding: All 14 assigned behavioral tests passed with exit code 0 in the isolated copy.

Recorder durations are calculated from server UTC start/stop timestamps. A stopped 25-second attempt retains 25 seconds after 90 additional seconds of observation entry. Repeated finish requests are rejected without changing duration.

Participant codes, device description, approved task and operator consent confirmation are required. One attempt per participant/task and a five-person cohort are enforced. Results remain Pending until all 10 attempts have final observations; success thresholds are inclusive at 120 and 60 seconds.

Locker readings are constrained to source SIMULATED. Invalid notice references are rejected, heartbeat preserves state, the ten-second open warning appears, and reset retains historical events after a notice becomes unavailable.
Admin access and CSRF checks pass; CSV formula-like entries are escaped; feature activity leaves the main database unchanged.

The packaged data folder contains only campus.sqlite3. No packaged research.sqlite3 or telemetry.sqlite3 exists. These tests create temporary fixtures with an injected clock and clean them afterward; they are not genuine human participant observations.
concrete_findings.evidence: data folder inspection; test_stage2_features.py setUpClass/setUp/tearDownClass; research template explicitly excludes automated tests and team rehearsals

limitations: Automated technical validation only. No real outside participants were recruited, observed, or counted, and no human usability success criteria were established by this review.
Timer behavior was verified using an injected deterministic test clock. The production path uses current UTC timestamps; no real elapsed-time human task was run.
The real-volunteer checkbox is an operator declaration, not independent verification of participant identity, consent, completion, or absence of coaching.
Timers use wall-clock UTC rather than a monotonic clock. Backward clock movement is rejected, but this suite does not test forward clock jumps.
All locker telemetry is simulated local SQLite data. No sensor, hardware, door operation, network, or physical item ownership/presence was verified.
No browser UI interaction or accessibility review was performed. The assigned 14-test suite is not an exhaustive audit.
